items: The epicenter is the first point on the Earth's surface to experience seismic body waves.
Shallow-focus earthquakes produce maximum destruction because seismic waves lose less energy before reaching the surface.
Deep-focus earthquakes occur almost exclusively along convergent boundaries along Wadati-Benioff zones.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Focus (or Hypocenter) is the location beneath the Earth's surface where tectonic stress is released and seismic energy originates.
The Epicenter is the point on the Earth's surface directly perpendicular to and vertically above the focus.
Earthquakes are classified by focal depth into shallow (0–70 km), intermediate (70–300 km), and deep (300–700 km).
Shallow-focus earthquakes account for the majority of global seismic activity and cause the most catastrophic destruction.
Deep-focus earthquakes occur primarily in subduction zones where oceanic plates sink into the mantle.
